name: Córdoba
tagline: The great mosque, flower-filled patios and Moorish lanes
summary: Córdoba was once the largest city in Western Europe and the capital of Islamic Spain. Walk the forest of red-and-white arches in the Mezquita, cross the Roman bridge at sunset, peek into flower-filled patios in the old Jewish quarter and ride out to the ruined palace city of Medina Azahara.
seasonNote: Spring is best, and May brings the patio festival; July and August often pass 40°C.
arrival: High-speed AVE trains reach Córdoba from Madrid in 1h45 and from Seville in 45 minutes; the station is a 20-minute walk from the old town.
gettingAround: The old town is small and walkable; take a bus or tour to Medina Azahara.
cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; small change helps at tapas bars. Tipping is optional, rounding up is enough.
foodTip: Salmorejo (thick cold tomato soup), flamenquín (rolled fried pork and ham) and rabo de toro (oxtail stew).
buyTip: Embossed leather (guadamecí) and silver filigree from the Judería workshops.

connections.note: AVE high-speed trains several times an hour.

items.name: Mosque–Cathedral (Mezquita)
items.summary: A vast 8th-century mosque of striped horseshoe arches with a Renaissance cathedral built into its heart.
items.expect: Paid; mass times close it to visitors on Sunday mornings.
items.tip: Come at the free early-morning entry (Mon to Sat, 8:30 to 9:20) for near silence.
